chapters.title: One Cambridge pathway, Grade 7 to Grade 12
chapters.lede: The Curriculum Module is not three separate programmes. It is one continuous design in three grade bands, where each band prepares students directly for the next.

blocks.lead: A student who moves through all three bands reaches Grade 12 having built the **same skills — critical thinking, structured writing, mathematical reasoning — at higher and higher levels**, using the same command words throughout.
points: **Grades 7–8** — Cambridge Lower Secondary, ending in the **Checkpoint**.
**Grades 9–10** — **IGCSE**. Grade 9 is Year 1 of IGCSE, not the end of SMP.
**Grades 11–12** — **AS Level** is the standard; full A Level is an extra continuation pathway.
National obligations are planned **alongside** Cambridge — never by removing required Cambridge content.
check: one continuous academic pathway from Grade 7 through Grade 12
Grade 9 treated as Year 1 of IGCSE

blocks.title: The pathway at a glance

steps.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
steps.text: Accelerated **Stage 7–9** sequence: Stage 8 is split across both years so Stage 9 is done by the end of Grade 8.

steps.name: Lower Secondary Checkpoint
steps.text: English, Mathematics, Science. **May** is the network default from 2026/2027.

steps.name: IGCSE
steps.text: Grade 9 = **Year 1 of IGCSE**. Grade 10 completes the cycle, with support for students who join with gaps.

steps.name: AS Level
steps.text: Four AS subjects: three pathway subjects + **General Paper (8021)**.

steps.name: AS examinations
steps.text: Students who continue to **A Level** sit it in the Grade 12 May/June series — in addition to the four AS, never instead.

source.at: The Three Bands; Key Policy Points

blocks.title: Grade 10: two classes, one destination
blocks.intro: For students who join Grade 10 without the Grade 9 IGCSE foundation.

steps.title: Placement test
steps.text: Every incoming new student, before the year starts. It checks English level, not only subject content. School of origin alone is never the criterion.

steps.title: Intensive or Regular
steps.text: Intensive: normal Grade 10 lessons + after-school and Saturday catch-up, **max 6 hours a week** extra. Regular: the standard programme.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Intensive placement is reviewed after **six weeks** and again at the end of Term 1.

source.at: The Two-Class Structure; Movement Between Classes

check: must not exceed 6 instructional hours per week
Intensive placement is reviewed after six weeks
Parent request alone is not a placement criterion

blocks.title: Why May for Checkpoint
blocks.text: A **May** sitting completes Checkpoint before Grade 9 begins, so students start IGCSE with full attention. Each Checkpoint series has **one fixed week with no make-up date**, and an October sitting would fall in the most disruptive weeks of the new school year.

source.at: Policy: May Series is the Default

check: A May sitting completes Checkpoint before Grade 9 begins

chapters.title: Choosing IGCSE and AS subjects well
chapters.lede: A strong choice is informed, not rushed. It balances interest, readiness, future direction, workload and what the school can realistically offer.

items.label: IGCSE subjects
items.note: Network default: 3 core (Bahasa Indonesia 0538, Mathematics 0580, the school's English route) + 3 pathway subjects.

items.label: AS subjects
items.note: Three approved pathway subjects + English General Paper (8021) for every student.

items.label: standard AS tracks
items.note: Engineering · Business · Medical. Other combinations through individual counselling.

blocks.title: How a subject choice is made

steps.title: Student & family
steps.text: Name interests, questions and possible future directions.

steps.title: Subject teachers
steps.text: Explain what the subject really demands and give an evidence-based readiness recommendation.

steps.title: Whole-combination check
steps.text: Workload, progression and school feasibility. Borderline or unusual cases are recorded.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.text: Final choices go on the official IGCSE or AS Level Subject Selection Form.

blocks.title: Good advice for families
do: Use the Cambridge syllabus for the year the student will **sit** the exam.
Look at several kinds of evidence — grades, Common Assessments, classwork, study habits.
Check a target university's **current official** entry requirements.
dont: Choosing because of friends, teacher preference, or because a subject seems “easier”.
Relying on memory or a generic pathway chart for university requirements.
Treating Additional Mathematics as simply “more of the same”.
check: Always use the Cambridge syllabus for the calendar year in which the student will sit the examination
Do not rely on memory or a generic pathway chart

blocks.title: Coming in AY 2027–2028
blocks.text: Ministry guidance says formative and summative results should not be combined into one number. This year's 40/30/20/10 stays. From **AY 2027–2028** the **Subject Grade** will use approved summative evidence only, and formative evidence will be reported separately as a **Learning Profile**.

blocks.title: Below KKTP? Re-teach, then one reassessment
blocks.text: Targeted re-teaching first, then **one reassessment within 10 working days** on the missed objectives only. The recorded grade is **capped at the KKTP**. EASE Growth is never part of the subject grade.

chapters.title: Keeping the curriculum on track all year
chapters.lede: Plan → Teach → Check coverage → Assess → Analyse → Intervene → Review → Improve. Use the Implementation Toolkit every semester, and resolve issues before they become year-end problems.

blocks.title: Who decides what

Day-to-day delivery: coverage, pacing, assessment readiness, transitions, placement and subject selection.
Subject quality: schemes of work, assessment quality, coaching, moderation support.
Network standards, approved exceptions, weighting and structure changes, annual curriculum review.
Final sign-off on major academic exceptions and network-wide standards.

blocks.title: Common questions

items.q: Can our school choose the March or October Checkpoint series?
items.a: Only as an exception agreed in advance with the Academic Board, after checking current Cambridge deadlines. May is the network default from 2026/2027.

items.q: Does every student have to follow one of the three AS tracks?
items.a: No. Engineering, Business and Medical are standard combinations. Students with other university targets take English General Paper plus three approved subjects chosen through individual counselling.
Only with written Academic Board approval before the academic year starts. The request comes through the Academic Coordinator with the proposed weighting, the rationale and a communication plan.

items.q: A parent wants their child in the Regular Grade 10 class. Is that enough?
items.a: No. The Academic Coordinator decides from the placement evidence and review criteria. A parent request alone is not a placement criterion.

items.q: Is the Cambridge Learning Objectives spreadsheet the syllabus?
items.a: No. It is a searchable planning aid and coverage varies by subject and grade. The current official Cambridge syllabus or framework is always the authority.

items.q: Does EASE Growth affect a student's subject grade?
items.a: No. It is not entered in the gradebook and never contributes to a subject grade.
